title: Federal ban on selling, purchasing or trading drug samples, and who may receive them
rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 353(c)(1), no person may sell, purchase, or trade or offer to sell, purchase, or trade any drug sample, a drug sample being a unit of a prescription drug which is not intended to be sold and is intended to promote the sale of the drug. Under 21 U.S.C. 353(d)(1), except as provided in paragraphs (2) and (3), no person may distribute any drug sample, and distribute does not include providing a sample to a patient by a practitioner licensed to prescribe the drug, a health care professional acting at the direction and under the supervision of such a practitioner, or a pharmacy of a hospital or other health care entity acting at the direction of such a practitioner that received the sample under paragraph (2) or (3). Under 21 U.S.C. 353(d)(2) and (3) and 21 CFR 203.30(a) and 203.31(a), a manufacturer or authorized distributor of record may distribute drug samples, by mail or common carrier or by a representative or detailer, to practitioners licensed to prescribe the drug or, at the written request of a licensed practitioner, to the pharmacy of a hospital or other health care entity, on a written request received before delivery and with a receipt signed by the recipient on delivery. 21 CFR 203.3 defines a health care entity as a person that provides diagnostic, medical, surgical, or dental treatment, or chronic or rehabilitative care, but not any retail pharmacy or wholesale distributor. Under 21 CFR 203.38(c) each sample unit bears a label clearly denoting its status as a drug sample, such as sample, not for sale, or professional courtesy package. Under 21 U.S.C. 331(t) the sale, purchase or trade of a drug sample in violation of 353(c) and the distribution of a drug sample in violation of 353(d) are prohibited acts.
exam_relevance: Tests the sample channel precisely: no sale, purchase or trade by anyone; distribution only to prescribers or, on a prescriber's written request, to a hospital or health care entity pharmacy; and a retail pharmacy is outside the definition of health care entity.

exceptions: Providing a sample to a patient by a licensed practitioner, by a health care professional at the practitioner's direction and under supervision, or by a hospital or health care entity pharmacy acting at a practitioner's direction that received it under 353(d)(2) or (3), is not a distribution.
21 CFR 203.39 separately permits a charitable institution to receive and dispense donated drug samples under stated conditions.
common_confusions: A retail pharmacy is not a health care entity, so it is not among the permitted recipients of samples.
The sale ban reaches purchase and trade and offers to do any of them, whoever the person is.
